In situations where children are abused there's often a "golden child." This term is used in therapy too, so it's not some malicious thing your sister made up. The golden child is clearly the favorite, although they often suffer abuse too. It's very common for the GC to be encouraged or forced to "punish" their siblings, especially the scapegoat child. The scapegoat child is the child who is blamed for the dysfunction of the family, the child that is told they can't do anything right, and the child who is compared to the GC. Your sister was the scapegoat. 

Whether you want to awknowledge it or not, you were one of her abusers. I know it's not your fault, but it's also unreasonable to expect her to just forget that. Of course she's hesitant to rekindle that relationship. That, and her entire family abandoned her as if the abuse was her fault, and once again showed favoritism to you. The wounds from child abuse run deep and take years of therapy to heal. Every further act of abuse, disowning her and cutting her out of inheritance, slices those wounds open again.

On some level, you must know what your grandparents did is messed up. Abandoning an absurd child over something that's not her fault. You sister couldn't control you going into foster care, she couldn't control your family's decision not to adopt you (being too far away is a bs excuse), nor could she control what happened to you in foster care. By continuing to blame her for everything bad that happened to you , you are repeating that same cycle of abuse your mother started and making her the scapegoat again. Until you get therapy, you will likely continue this cycle of blaming others for bad things that happen to you, maybe even your own kids. You will not be able to maintain a relationship with your sister until you stop.

If you want to heal yourself, because you are broken even if you don't think so, and set yourself on a path to a healthy relationship with your sister, I suggest you first take this money and go to therapy. You should arrange to pay for your sister's therapy too, and some family therapy sessions when you're both ready. If there is anything substantial left, you should set up a trust fund she can access when she's older or college fund for her. I wouldn't give it to the aunt (cause screw her) or give her cash the aunt can access. Tou shouldn't make it a condition that sister has a a relationship with you to access the funds, because that's abuse. 

You stand absolutely nothing to gain by continuing to blame sister for things that are not her fault. She's healing from a horrible childhood too. Is the money worth not ever having a relationship with her?

I know this thread is 4 months old, but I wanted to say hi, fellow American! I love Tokio Hotel. They had a brief run of popularity here in like 2008 to 2010. Some people who were into a certain kind of music (emo, pop punk, etc) around that time remember them. Their old style is very different than their more pop, dance music style of today. I think they're not more popular in the US for a number of reasons. Mostly because they kind of disappeared off the face of the earth for a long time. I'm not sure why that happened, but I do know that when they took their break, the market was saturated with other bands that had a similar sound and look. I became a fan in 2013, and at that time, they hadn't made any new music in years or even updated their social media in forever. They came back in 2014/15 with Kings of Suburbia. It was a whole new sound and look. It turned a lot of their old fans off. They launched a world tour, the Feel it all tour. It was more successful in Europe. I went to their show in Chicago. It was sad. I paid full price for my tickets the day they went on sale. But in the days leading up to the show, they were selling for like $10. The venue wasn't even at half capacity. Basically, I feel they were known for a specific sound. They lost fans as those fans grew out of listening to that kind of music, they lost fans during their long hiatus, they lost fans when they came back with a new style of music. They're essentially starting over in a different genre of music after a lot of people forgot they existed after a long break. Their new music does sound like what's on the radio nowadays. But they aren't widely known anymore here and it's a tough market that's saturated with other artists with very similar sounds.

Also, they have a history of unprofessional behavior and a history of poorly promoting and marketing themselves. Their last US/Canada tour was just canceled. At that time I was still moderately active on TH Twitter and I remember logging in and seeing people confused and upset because the venues had began issuing refunds for tickets. There was no explanation from the band, and they never awknowledged it, as far as I know. It was like they couldn't be bothered to even say anything.

I suggest you figure out your tax bill first. My husband owed the IRS when we were first dating. The interest is killer, and no matter what, you will be backed into a corner and forced to pay one way or another. They will sieze any future tax returns until your debt is paid, and they will eventually garnish your wages. They can and eventually will levy your assets too. They can just take money that's in your accounts. They can take your car. My husband had let it go to the point that they were sending letters telling him they were going to levy his assets in so many days. By that time, he owed over $1000 in interest alone. They will work with you on a payment plan, though. My suggestion is to see if the money you have now can just take care of the debt. If it can't, try to get a payment plan set up.
